rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 6 'Two artefacts from one ticket' line 52, 'The loop that started with a failing test closed.' 'The loop' is never named earlier inside THIS file, but the rule's module-include-order clause makes the enclosing module's own signposting count as prior deck-order context: getting-going.md line 16, under '## What You'll Learn' (which precedes '## Start here' at line 36 where this exercise is included), reads '**Run** an orient -> fix -> close -> compound loop end-to-end on a trivial bug in your own repo' -- verified live against the current file, not carried from any cache. That bullet is the resolving antecedent, sitting before this exercise in deck order; 'the loop' is a plain definite-article callback to it, not a broken referent. (getting-going.md's Key Concepts line 57 restates the same loop but sits AFTER '## Start here' in that file's own order, so it is not needed as the antecedent and isn't cited as one.) Chunk 0/1's 'the bug you fixed' (lines 5, 13) and the expanded prompt's 'the PR' (chunk 3, prompt at line 39) resolve under the session-artifact carve-out ('the failing test', 'the PR' are both named in the carve-out's own example list). Chunk 4's 'it' (line 43) is immediate continuation of chunk 3's close-out subject. Chunk 5's 'the next agent' (line 48) is generic future-session phrasing needing no specific antecedent, and is maintainer-attested (line 115) as Antti's own working frame. No never-named or vague-with-full-history referent found.

Only external pointer in body: chunk 3 line 35, '[MCP and connectors](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md)' -- named by the document's own title in the same sentence ('Adding a connector is one command per tracker'), not located by page position. Satisfies the navigational-pointer carve-out. No 'the opening lecture said' / positional-callback pattern anywhere in the body (lines 1-55).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Backward references: chunk 1's 'the bug you fixed' (line 13) and chunk 6's 'a failing test' (line 52) both resolve against fix-tests-first.md. Verified live via getting-going.md '## Start here' include order (lines 44-50): orient-and-introspect.md -> fix-tests-first.md -> close-the-ticket.md -> compound-and-close.md -- fix-tests-first (which ships the PR via TDD) is the exercise immediately preceding this one, matching this file's own maintainer line 60 ('Runs after fix-tests-first (the PR is shipped)'). No dead beat references.

Shortest chunk is 4, 'Double-check the voice' (lines 41-44): its one bullet ('Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket? If the wording feels off or wrong, tell Claude which line and how you'd write it.') is a self-sufficient compare-and-correct instruction, not a bare wait-state. All six body chunks carry a self-contained instruction or claim; none merely restates a context-dependent fragment.

Checked all six headers against their own chunk content: 'Read the ticket for your bug' (11-19) -> opens+pastes ticket link; 'Read the conventions off the ticket' (20-31) -> field-convention read + five-rule ask; 'Write the close-out and send it' (33-40) -> drafts+posts close-out; 'Double-check the voice' (41-44) -> register check; 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' (45-49) -> generalises the move (declarative, cleared under rule 15); 'Two artefacts from one ticket' (50-55) -> names the two artefacts (close-out note, conventions) that the paragraph beneath it lists. No header contradicted by its own chunk.

Checked all five sub-items across all six chunks. 'Not X. Not Y. Z.': grep for standalone 'Not ' sentence-openers in the body -> 0 hits (only 'not the policy' L23 and 'did not write' L47, both single negations mid-sentence). Anaphora/epistrophe triples: none found on a full read. Self-grading-superlative sub-item (blocking): closest line is chunk 3 L35, '...and it pays back on every session after this one' -- a persistence claim about the connector install, not graded/superlative language ('most useful', 'one of the best'); stays inside. Number+retraction: 'five bug rules' (L27/31) and '20 minutes' (L3) stay unhedged. Abstraction-noun stacks: none -- vocabulary stays concrete (ticket, tracker, connector, close-out, comments). Empty-leg verb triplets: none found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Five of six body headings are imperative or a recap/phase-label form: 'Read the ticket for your bug', 'Read the conventions off the ticket', 'Write the close-out and send it', 'Double-check the voice', and the closer 'Two artefacts from one ticket' (a catalogue-style label naming its own subject, the NOT-violation shape the rule names -- e.g. 'The numbers'). Chunk 5's 'Anything can be reverse-engineered' (line 45) is the file's one deliberate declarative -- it is one of the compendium's own two named corpus specimens for this exact heading in this exact file (rule 15's 2026-08-15 measurement note), landing at the moment the exercise generalises past its own task. Earned exception, not drift.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every bullet/closer sentence against the three classes. Closest candidate: chunk 6 line 52, 'Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note on the bug you shipped, and the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along.' -- reads as a recap, but it names two CONCRETE outputs (a close-out note, a set of conventions) rather than re-announcing an abstract split/lens already stated, so it clears class (a). Line 52's second sentence ('The loop that started with a failing test closed.') and line 54 ('The field rules stay in the scrollback. The next exercise sweeps this whole session.') each add a distinct functional fact (arc closure; where the rules currently live and what happens to them next, matching the no-fold-step note at maintainer line 60) rather than restating the header or the widget's '**The point:**' line (line 9, a different claim about reverse-engineering). No doctrine restatement, self-referential design commentary, or hollow aphorism kicker found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file's own closer is the rule's cited PASS calibration ('close-the-ticket.md "Two artefacts from one ticket" names what its recap already held'). Verified against the live commit, not the cache: `git show de4a638d -- curriculum/exercises/close-the-ticket.md` shows the header changed from '## What happened' to '## Two artefacts from one ticket' on 2026-09-03 with the body paragraph beneath it UNCHANGED -- the commit message states 'the body's own first sentence had the specific ready.' Covering the new header and reading only the body: 'a close-out note on the bug you shipped, and the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along' already answers 'what were the two artefacts' with no inherited bullet answering the old label-header's job.
